samuel1.14.p1.b1.text: “Come, let us cross over to the Philistine outpost on the other side.”

samuel1.14.p1.b2.text: But Jonathan did not tell his father. Meanwhile, Saul was staying … on the outskirts of Gibeah. And the troops who were with him numbered about six hundred men …

samuel1.14.p1.b3.text: But the troops did not know that Jonathan had left.

samuel1.14.p1.b4.text: Now there were cliffs on both sides of the pass … One was named Bozez and the other Seneh.

samuel1.14.p2.b1.text: … Perhaps the LORD will work on our behalf. Nothing can hinder the LORD from saving, whether by many or by few.

samuel1.14.p2.b2.text: “Do all that is in your heart. Go ahead; I am with you heart and soul.”

samuel1.14.p2.b3.text: But if they say, ‘Come on up,’ then we will go up, because this will be our sign …

samuel1.14.p3.b1.text: So the two of them showed themselves to the outpost of the Philistines

samuel1.14.p3.b2.text: “Look, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes in which they were hiding!”

samuel1.14.p3.b3.text: “Come on up, and we will teach you a lesson!”

samuel1.14.p3.b4.text: “Follow me,” Jonathan told his armor-bearer, “for the LORD has delivered them into the hand of Israel.”

samuel1.14.p4.b1.text: So Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer behind him.

samuel1.14.p4.b2.text: In that first assault, Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about twenty men …

samuel1.14.p4.b3.text: Then terror struck the Philistines in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. … Indeed, the earth quaked and panic spread from God.

samuel1.14.p5.b1.text: … Saul’s watchmen at Gibeah in Benjamin looked and saw the troops melting away and scattering in every direction

samuel1.14.p5.b2.text: “Call the roll and see who has left us.”

samuel1.14.p6.b1.text: … they found the Philistines in total confusion, with each man wielding the sword against his neighbor.

samuel1.14.p6.b2.text: And the Hebrews who had previously gone up into the surrounding camps of the Philistines now went over to the Israelites …

samuel1.14.p6.b3.text: So the LORD saved Israel that day, and the battle moved on beyond Beth-aven.

samuel1.14.p7.b1.text: Saul had placed the troops under an oath, saying, “Cursed is the man who eats any food before evening, before I have taken vengeance on my enemies.”

samuel1.14.p7.b2.text: Now the men of Israel were in distress that day … So none of the troops tasted any food.

samuel1.14.p7.b3.text: Then all the troops entered the forest, and there was honey on the ground.

samuel1.14.p7.b4.text: … not one of them put his hand to his mouth, because they feared the oath.

samuel1.14.p8.b1.text: Jonathan, however, had not heard that his father had charged the people with the oath. So he reached out the end of the staff in his hand, dipped it into the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes brightened.

samuel1.14.p8.b2.text: “Your father bound the troops with a solemn oath, saying, ‘Cursed is the man who eats food today.’ That is why the people are faint.”

samuel1.14.p8.b3.text: “My father has brought trouble to the land,” Jonathan replied. “Just look at how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.

samuel1.14.p8.b4.text: How much better it would have been if the troops had eaten freely today from the plunder they took from their enemies! Would not the slaughter of the Philistines have been much greater?”

samuel1.14.p9.b1.text: That day, after the Israelites had struck down the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon, the people were very faint.

samuel1.14.p9.b2.text: So they rushed greedily to the plunder, taking sheep, cattle, and calves. They slaughtered them on the ground and ate meat with the blood still in it.

samuel1.14.p9.b3.text: “You have broken faith,” said Saul. “Roll a large stone over here at once.”

samuel1.14.p9.b4.text: Then Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first time he had built an altar to the LORD.

samuel1.14.p10.b1.text: “Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder them until dawn, leaving no man alive!”

samuel1.14.p10.b2.text: So Saul inquired of God … But God did not answer him that day.

samuel1.14.p10.b3.text: … even if it is my son Jonathan, he must die!”

samuel1.14.p10.b4.text: And Jonathan and Saul were selected … And Jonathan was selected.

samuel1.14.p11.b1.text: “I only tasted a little honey with the end of the staff that was in my hand. And now I must die?”

samuel1.14.p11.b2.text: “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if you, Jonathan, do not surely die!”

samuel1.14.p11.b3.text: “Must Jonathan die—he who accomplished such a great deliverance for Israel? Never! … not a hair of his head will fall to the ground …

samuel1.14.p11.b4.text: Then Saul gave up his pursuit of the Philistines, and the Philistines returned to their own land.

samuel1.14.p12.b1.text: After Saul had assumed the kingship over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side … Wherever he turned, he routed them.

samuel1.14.p12.b2.text: He fought valiantly and defeated the Amalekites, delivering Israel from the hands of its plunderers.

samuel1.14.p12.b3.text: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua. His two daughters were named Merab (his firstborn) and Michal (his younger daughter).

samuel1.14.p12.b4.text: And the war with the Philistines was fierce for all the days of Saul. So whenever he noticed any strong or brave man, Saul would enlist him.
